benefits.title: Meet the movie you opened.
benefits.body: Identify movies and TV episodes from filenames and folders. View artwork, overview, cast, and crew in a Metadata sidebar.

benefits.title: Check the match first.
benefits.body: Fix an uncertain match by title, year, or type. Review exactly what will be written before pressing Save to file.

benefits.title: Let the details travel.
benefits.body: Write tags into supported video files, and save .nfo files and artwork alongside them for your other media apps.

workflowTitle: A better library starts with one file.
workflowIntro: Open a local video in IINA, then choose Plugin → Metadata → Show Metadata. The plugin looks for a match and shows what it found.

examples.title: Recognise
examples.body: Title and year help identify a movie. Episodes can use S01E02 or a season-folder layout.

examples.title: Review
examples.body: Choose the right title and review the “Will write” list in the sidebar.

examples.title: Save
examples.body: Save embedded tags and the selected sidecar files. Nothing is written until you choose to save.

installSteps.body: In IINA, go to Settings → Plugins → Install from GitHub and enter:

installSteps.title: Connect TMDB
installSteps.body: Open Plugin → Metadata → Show Metadata and add your TMDB API Read Access Token. TV episodes can use TVmaze without a token.

installSteps.title: Review and save
installSteps.body: Check the match and the “Will write” list, then choose Save to file. Nothing changes until you save.

faqs.a: No. It shows a match and a list of proposed writes. You must press Save to file. Existing sidecars and artwork are moved to Trash when replaced, unless you choose to keep them.

faqs.q: Does it work with Infuse or Kodi?
faqs.a: It supports Infuse-style and Kodi/Jellyfin-style sidecar names. In Infuse, enable Prefer Local Artwork. Infuse uses movie .nfo files, but ignores TV .nfo files. Embedded metadata also depends on Infuse’s metadata-fetching settings.
Search terms derived from filenames/folders and IDs are sent to TMDB or TVmaze. Videos are not uploaded. The TMDB token stays in Keychain; responses are cached locally for a week.
Replaced sidecars and artwork are in Trash. Original MKV tags are backed up once. MP4 files do not keep a backup; check the proposed changes before saving. See the README for recovery instructions.

Only local files are supported. Air-date episode filenames are not recognised; use S01E02 or a season folder. Multi-episode files get the first episode’s metadata. An MP4 rewrite can need free space about the size of the file.

interactiveDemo: The preview shows an IINA player window with the real Metadata sidebar. Use the Metadata button or Plugin → Metadata → Show Metadata to reveal the sidebar, correct the Spring match, and try Save to file. Player controls use poster artwork and a simulated timeline; no video or audio is streamed. Metadata searches and saves use an in-memory bridge, without provider requests or file writes.
